claims.text: Ab initio molecular dynamics with explicit oxygen-impurity modeling can predict lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions separately in HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicit defect and impurity modeling will outperform earlier analytical approaches by capturing their effects on heat transport.
The proposed approach provides a more accurate description of phonon-electron interactions than earlier approaches.
The proposed approach is expected to reduce the mean absolute error of thermal-conductivity predictions by 15% relative to DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates.
The modeled material is HfNbTaTiZr containing possible defects or impurities, including approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed simulation explicitly models oxygen impurities.
The claimed applicability range is 100–1200 K.
The claimed sample applicability range includes oxygen contents of 0.1–1 wt.%.
The claimed sample applicability range includes defect densities of 10^15–10^18 cm^-3.
Atomic-scale defects and impurities, including oxygen vacancies or interstitials, are the proposed structural mediator.
The proposed heat-transport mechanism involves phonon-electron interactions and scattering by defects and impurities.
The predicted lattice thermal conductivity at 300 K is 5–10 W/(K m).
The predicted electronic thermal conductivity at 300 K is 5–7 W/(K m).
The predicted total thermal conductivity is 10–17 W/(K m) over 300–1200 K.
The predicted total conductivity will be within 10% of experimental measurements.
Experimental total conductivity is 10–17 W/(K m) from 300 to 1200 K.
Other impurities or defects may alter predictive accuracy.
The falsification experiment compares predictions against samples spanning 0.1–1 wt.% oxygen and 10^15–10^18 cm^-3 defect density, plus a minimal-defect and minimal-impurity control.
The hypothesis is falsified if either separated contribution deviates by more than 20% from experiment.
The hypothesis is falsified if total conductivity deviates by more than 15% from experiment.
